rules.title: Newark municipal rent control ordinance (unverified)
rules.requirement: Newark is believed to regulate rent increases through a municipal rent control ordinance, as New Jersey allows municipalities to do. The ordinance text was not captured, so the cap, covered buildings and exemptions are unverified.
rules.citation: Newark Mun. Code, rent control ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Municipalities may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied or small-building exemptions under the local ordinance

rules.conflict_note: Unverified: based on link-only Newark code sources (D070-D072) whose text could not be read. The quoted span comes from D067 (NJ DCA Truth in Renting guide) and supports only the general proposition that NJ municipalities may adopt rent control.
rules.review_note: Specific section, cap formula and exemptions not stated in the provided documents. The 30-year new-construction exemption comes from N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5, as described in D067.

parsed.notes: No candidates were supplied for Newark. All provided documents are state-level (NJ FAIR Act, Fair Chance in Housing Act, application-fee cap, DCA guide), so they are not duplicated here. The only Newark rule I added is the rent control ordinance, as an unverified link-only record. Newark's code text was not captured for the other categories, so I did not add rules there.
